name: Solid Windlassdrum
description: Plant both feet wide behind the stock and lock the knees so the release cannot rock the body.

name: Kind Stockbed
description: Turn the winch handle with both hands to a steady count until the string rides home against the catch.

name: Clawcount
description: Lay the bolt shaft along the groove with the fletching flat and the head seated against the slider.

name: Watching Claw
description: Close one eye and sight along the spine of the stock to line the bolt head on the mark.

name: Stiff Bowarms
description: Squeeze the trigger lever at the bottom of the breath so the bolt leaves flat and without a jerk.

name: Measured Aimframe
description: Alternate hand over hand on the winch bar, hauling the cord back a notch at a time without slackening.

name: Gentle Trackbed
description: Listen for each pawl tooth to seat in the ratchet so the winder knows the string has not slipped.

name: Slider Count
description: Drive the hip into the lever arm instead of the shoulder, spending the whole body's weight on the last turns.

name: Blunt Springarm
description: Swing the iron winch bar short and hard across the wrist of anyone reaching for the loaded engine.

name: Judging Sinewcord
description: Ease the lever back one tooth at a time to unload a drawn string when the shot is called off.

name: Kept Aimframe
description: Wedge the heel behind the carriage wheel and lean back, holding the engine steady against a shove from the front.

name: Calm Slider
description: Carry the bolt cradled along the forearm with the head forward, so it reaches the groove without a fumble.

name: Sideways Boltflight
description: Step to the bolt rack with the near foot and draw one shaft in a single reach, eyes still on the engine.

name: Stakereview
description: Run a thumb along the fletching and nock end to find a bent vane before the bolt is laid.

name: Stakecount
description: Push the bolt headfirst along the groove until the shaft bumps the string and cannot slide back.

name: Sliderreview
description: Shout the clearing word and look both ways down the line, confirming that no body stands in the bolt's path.

name: Tending Bolthead
description: Lay three spare bolts fanned on the ground at the right hand so the next load needs no search.

name: Stiff Stakedrive
description: Drive the shoulder into a rushing man at the loading side to knock him off his feet.

name: Shifting Hurtle
description: Shove the stock a quarter turn around its pivot post with both palms, bringing the bolt line onto a new target.

name: Slidergauge
description: Tap the wooden wedge under the rear of the stock with a mallet until the nose rises by a finger's width.

name: Deep Sinewcord
description: Wiggle the iron pivot pin and press on the mount collar to feel for play before a shot.

name: Stakewedge
description: Lean a shoulder against the mount post and crouch behind the stock, using the timber to shelter the head.

name: Descending Streak
description: Swing the stock across a moving target on its pivot and release the instant the bolt line crosses the mark.

name: Backward Claw
description: Three crew push the carriage wheels together on a shouted count to roll the engine forward over rough ground.

name: Settled Stockbed
description: Drop the carriage trail and kick the chocks under the wheels so the engine stands fixed for firing.

name: Even Springarm
description: The aimer and the loader call each step aloud in turn so that no step is skipped under pressure.

name: Stakebump
description: On the crew chief's count the aimer releases, and the loader is already reaching for the next bolt.

name: Sideways Streak
description: Throw a rope loop over the shoulder and drag the unloaded engine along the track one lurching step at a time.

name: Descending Bolthead
description: Drive the rear end of the stock backward into an attacker at the engine's tail to break his rush.

name: Warm Bowarms
description: Draw a thin thread of qi along each twisted skein and read which arm is the stiffer before the shot.

name: Warm Stockbed
description: Wind both torsion arms back together with qi evenly in both hands so neither arm leads the other.

name: Solid Aimframe
description: Swing the iron spanner up and across to turn a spear point off its line toward the engine.

name: Steady Windlassdrum
description: Press a breath of qi into the string loop as it seats on the catch, firming the hold.

name: Flat Impalement
description: Release the trigger and let both arms whip forward together, throwing the bolt flat down the groove.

name: Stakehit
description: Lower the nose until the groove runs level, then loose the bolt point blank across an open courtyard.

name: Clawstay
description: Hold the wound arms at full draw while a breath of qi steadies the straining frame during a long wait.

name: Slidernote
description: Ease the trigger forward with a thumb on the string so a drawn arm unloads with no bolt in the groove.

name: Judging Trackbed
description: Rest a thread of qi on the rear sight notch so the eye finds its centre every time.

name: Watching Bowarms
description: Hold the front pin a quarter-width above the mark to allow for the bolt's fall at middle range.

name: Short Hurtle
description: Settle the sight on the mark, let the breath fall away, and release in the empty moment.

name: Clawnote
description: Glance at a hanging ribbon, judge the crosswind, and shift the aim a hair upwind before firing.

name: Clawgauge
description: Reseat the next bolt by touch while the eyes stay on the target, so the second shot costs no time.

name: Gentle Windlassdrum
description: Dampen the sinew skeins with an oiled cloth in slow rounds so they keep their spring in dry air.

name: Judging Claw
description: Count the half turns put into the skein and mark each with a knot, keeping both sides alike.

name: Stakenote
description: Pass a breath of qi along a skein strand and note any fray where the flow stutters.

name: Hard Skewerbolt
description: Snap a loose skein end like a lash across the hand or face of a man beside the engine.

name: Deep Bolthead
description: Splice a spare strand into a worn skein with qi-warmed fingers so the engine can fire again soon.

name: Stakehusk
description: Hold the half-wound arms still with one palm and a breath of qi while a comrade fits the lever.

name: Mild Trackbed
description: Rub a thumb of wax along the groove floor so the bolt slides without catching or dragging.

name: Calm Sinewcord
description: Tap the bolt head with a knuckle and a pulse of qi to seat it firmly against the slider.

name: Clawreview
description: Feel the string claw settle on the nut through the stock, trusting touch over sight.

name: Gnawing Impalement
description: Take up the trigger slack in three parts, bleeding qi into the string until the release breaks clean.

name: Low Skewerbolt
description: Loose a bolt from a half-wound string when a target appears suddenly and the crew has no time to finish winding.

name: Stakegauge
description: Lay a flat blade across the groove to see that the stock is level before the bolt is loaded.

name: Solid Slider
description: Draw a bolt that failed to fly back out of the groove with the stock tilted safely downward.

name: Planted Sinewcord
description: Set the standing shield plank upright in front of the engine and brace it with the foot and a pulse of qi.

name: Measured Windlassdrum
description: Raise only the eyes above the pavise rim, scan the field, and drop back behind the plank.

name: Firm Springarm
description: Fire through the narrow slot between two pavises, keeping the bolt line flat and the head covered.

name: Stakepause
description: Tilt the pavise edge outward as a bolt strikes, glancing it away from the crew.

name: Swaying Stakedrive
description: Slide the engine along the line of pavises a plank-length at a time without exposing the flank.
